QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_48

question.text: The SAS Framework can be applied by mutual agreement to engagements where there are no intended users other than the reporting entity. In such cases, the SIA's report must:

answer.text: Be published on the Social Stock Exchange in all cases
Include a statement restricting the use of the report to the reporting entity
Be furnished to SEBI for approval before release
Be discussed first with the SIA's own SRO

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.6.2(c): 'The social impact assessors and the reporting entity may agree to apply the principles of this framework to an engagement when there are no intended users other than the reporting entity. In such situations, the social impact assessor's report includes a statement restricting the use of the report to the reporting entity.' The Trap: A wrongly requires SSE publication; C wrongly inserts SEBI pre-approval; D fabricates an SRO approval step. Cross-Exam Context: Restricted-use statements are standard in ICAI assurance engagements; XXIII imports the same convention. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Include the restriction paragraph right below the addressee — placing it in footnotes has led to reliance claims by unintended users, and at least one ICAI SIAB case centred on this very placement issue.
